Symptoms

Laptop cannot connect to corporate Wi-Fi network. Wi-Fi icon shows "No Internet" or "Limited Connectivity." The device connects briefly then disconnects, or fails to obtain an IP address.

Cause

Wi-Fi issues are commonly caused by expired or incorrect wireless credentials, wireless adapter driver issues, interference from other wireless networks, DHCP server exhaustion, or 802.1X authentication certificate expiration.

Resolution

  1. Forget the wireless network profile and reconnect with current credentials.
  2. Toggle airplane mode on and off to reset the wireless adapter.
  3. Update or reinstall the wireless adapter driver via Device Manager.
  4. Run the Windows Network Troubleshooter: Settings > Network & Internet > Status > Network troubleshooter.
  5. Verify the 802.1X certificate has not expired: check certificate store for the corporate CA certificate.

Workaround

Connect via ethernet cable if available. Alternatively, use a mobile hotspot for immediate internet access while troubleshooting the Wi-Fi issue.

Verification

  1. Connect to the corporate Wi-Fi and confirm "Connected" status with internet access.
  2. Run ipconfig and verify a valid IP address is assigned from the corporate DHCP range.
  3. Access an internal web application to confirm full network connectivity.
